status_summary: The statutory structure (six members, four votes to act) is unchanged, but seats were not filled as terms ended and the FEC has lacked a quorum since 2025-05-01. Commissioner Cooksey (R) left on 2025-01-20, the President removed Chair Weintraub (D) by letter on 2025-01-31 (a removal she and some members of Congress contest), Commissioner Dickerson (R) left at term end on 2025-04-30, and Commissioner Trainor (R) resigned effective 2025-10-03, leaving two Democrats. On 2026-02-11 the President nominated Ashley Stow and Andrew Woodson to the seats vacated by Trainor and Dickerson; the FEC chair said on 2026-04-30 that no one had been confirmed, and the FEC's commissioners page listed two commissioners on 2026-10-07. No nominee for the other two vacant seats, no holdover-limit bill and no administration position on odd-number proposals was found.

timeline.event: Commissioner Sean Cooksey (R) resigns to become counsel to the Vice President; five commissioners remain.
The President removes FEC Chair Ellen Weintraub (D), as reported by CRS; she and some members of Congress contest the removal's legality, and CRS does not analyze the dispute.

Executive order on accountability for independent regulatory agencies extends OIRA review of significant rules to those agencies and states that the President's and Attorney General's legal interpretations control within the executive branch, including in litigation; Democratic party committees later sued over its application to the FEC (see 2025-06-03). Context for presidential control of the FEC.
Commissioner Allen Dickerson (R) leaves at the end of his term; with three members left, the FEC loses its four-vote quorum as of 2025-05-01.

A federal judge dismisses a challenge by the DNC, DSCC and DCCC to the application of the independent-agencies order to the FEC, finding no live controversy because government lawyers said there was no plan to apply it to the FEC; the court left open a renewed claim.
Commissioner James Trainor (R) resignation, announced 2025-09-25, takes effect, leaving two Democratic commissioners (Broussard and Lindenbaum).
President nominates Ashley Stow (to the Trainor seat) and Andrew Woodson (to the Dickerson seat); if both were confirmed the FEC would regain four members, with two seats still vacant.
Senate Rules Committee Chairman McConnell issues a statement welcoming the nominees and a timely hearing; no hearing date is given.
FEC Chair Broussard marks one year without a quorum, the longest in the commission's history, and says no nominees have been confirmed.
